name: Gestao Hospital
description: We need an API to organize a public health system, specifically to assist the Unified Health System (SUS) in Brazil. The goal is to create a tool that helps avoid waste and optimize resources based on patient needs. The system should manage hospital information, including their stock of products, blood banks, and available beds. It should be able to recommend the closest hospital with available beds to a patient and facilitate the transfer of products, such as blood, between nearby hospitals if one is in need. A hospital with four or fewer items or liters of a product is considered to have only enough for its own use. The API should allow for registering hospitals, indicating the closest hospital to a patient's location, managing patient check-in and check-out, checking available beds, and managing product and blood bank inventories within hospitals.
highLevelGoals: The Public Health System Administrator aims to minimize waste and maximize the efficient use of resources (beds, products, blood) across all managed hospitals.
The Public Health System Administrator needs to ensure that all hospital data, including stock levels, blood bank status, and bed availability, is current and reliable for effective decision-making.
The Public Health System Administrator seeks to enable the seamless transfer of essential products, such as blood, between hospitals to address shortages and prevent critical situations.
Hospital Staff aims to efficiently manage and track the stock of products and blood bank inventories within their hospital to ensure availability and prevent shortages.
Hospital Staff seeks to efficiently manage patient admissions and discharges, ensuring accurate record-keeping and timely updates on bed availability.
Hospital Staff needs to quickly and accurately determine the number of available beds to manage patient flow and facilitate transfers.
The Patient aims to quickly and easily find a suitable hospital with available beds based on their current location and needs.
lowLevelGoals: The Public Health System Administrator needs to query the system to get the current inventory count for a particular product (e.g., masks, ventilators) from every hospital.
The Public Health System Administrator needs to access a dashboard or report showing the number of occupied and available beds in each department (e.g., ICU, general ward) for every hospital.
The Public Health System Administrator needs to view a consolidated report of the current stock of each blood type (e.g., A+, O-) in the blood banks of all managed hospitals.

The Public Health System Administrator needs to create analytical reports that show historical data on product consumption, bed occupancy rates, and blood usage to identify trends and inform future allocation strategies.
The Public Health System Administrator needs to be notified automatically when a hospital's stock of a critical product or blood type falls below a predefined threshold.
The Public Health System Administrator needs to be able to manually adjust or confirm the stock levels of products for a specific hospital in the system.
The Public Health System Administrator needs to be able to manually adjust or confirm the stock levels of blood types for a specific hospital's blood bank in the system.
The Public Health System Administrator needs to be able to manually update the number of available beds or the status of specific beds (e.g., occupied, vacant, out of service) for a hospital.
The Public Health System Administrator needs to check when the product inventory, blood bank, and bed availability data for a specific hospital was last updated to ensure its recency.

The Public Health System Administrator needs to initiate a request within the system to move a certain quantity of a product (e.g., medication, equipment) from a source hospital to a destination hospital.

The Public Health System Administrator needs to initiate a request within the system to move a certain quantity of a specific blood type from a source hospital's blood bank to a destination hospital's blood bank.
The Public Health System Administrator needs to review incoming transfer requests from other hospitals or system-generated recommendations and either approve or reject them.
The Public Health System Administrator needs to monitor the progress of initiated product and blood transfers, from initiation to delivery, within the system.
Hospital Staff needs to input details for a newly acquired product (e.g., name, quantity, expiration date) into the hospital's inventory system.
Hospital Staff needs to adjust the stock level of a specific product in the inventory system, reflecting new deliveries or usage.
Hospital Staff needs to delete a product record from the inventory system, for example, if it's discontinued or fully depleted and not being restocked.
Hospital Staff needs to add details of a newly received blood donation (e.g., blood type, quantity, donor information, collection date) to the blood bank system.
Hospital Staff needs to decrement the quantity of a specific blood type in the blood bank system when units are dispensed for patient use.
Hospital Staff needs to access a list showing the current stock of all products within their hospital, including quantities and locations.
Hospital Staff needs to access a list showing the current stock of all blood types in their hospital's blood bank, including quantities and expiration dates.
Hospital Staff needs to input a new patient's demographic information, medical history, and admission details into the system upon their arrival.
Hospital Staff needs to select an appropriate available bed from the system and link it to a newly admitted patient's record.
Hospital Staff needs to update a patient's status to 'discharged' in the system, record discharge details, and free up their assigned bed.
Hospital Staff needs to modify or add details to a patient's record (e.g., new diagnosis, treatment plan, transfer to another department) while they are admitted.
Hospital Staff needs to access a comprehensive list of all patients currently checked into the hospital, including their assigned beds and admission dates.
Hospital Staff needs to quickly see a summary count of all vacant beds across all departments within their hospital.
Hospital Staff needs to filter and see the number of available beds within a particular department (e.g., Emergency, Pediatrics) or a specific ward.
Hospital Staff needs to change the status of a specific bed in the system to reflect its current state, ensuring accurate availability information.
Hospital Staff needs to query the system to find beds that meet certain requirements, such as beds equipped for critical care or isolation.
The Patient needs to provide their current geographical coordinates to the system, either manually or via device GPS.
The Patient needs to input any specific requirements for a bed, such as 'ICU bed', 'pediatric bed', or 'cardiology department', to narrow down recommendations.
The Patient needs the system to return a ranked list of hospitals that have available beds matching their criteria, ordered by proximity.
The Patient needs to be able to select a recommended hospital and view its address, contact information, and specific bed availability details.
The Patient needs the system to provide navigation instructions to a chosen hospital from their current location.
